author: A student of the mountain, who did not give his name
pages:
#On Learning to Shout

I climbed the long stair to the monastery at the mountain's peak when I was nineteen, certain that I would learn the Voice within a year. I stayed eleven years. I learned a single word.

This book is about why that is not a failure.

#The First Lesson

My first lesson was silence. The masters did not speak to me for three months. They pointed, they nodded, they handed me a broom. I swept the courtyard until my hands blistered and the blisters healed and blistered again.

When at last the eldest master spoke, he said one thing: a word spoken carelessly is a wound in the world. Then he went back to his meditation.

#The Nature of the Words

A word of power is not merely a sound. To speak it truly you must understand it, the way you understand hunger or grief. The word for force is not a noise but a pushing; the word for fire is not a noise but a burning.

Mortals learn these words slowly, a little at a time, through years of reflection. The masters say there is another way, faster and far more dangerous, but they would not speak of it to me.

#The Walls

In ancient places across the north, the dragons carved their words into stone. Sometimes those walls seem to wake when a certain kind of traveller approaches, and the carved letters burn with light.

The masters became very quiet when I asked about this. One of them said only that the walls remember who they were made for.

#What I Carried Home

I came down from the mountain with one word and a great deal of patience. The word I have spoken aloud only twice. The patience I use every day.

If you seek the Voice, climb the stair. Bring warm boots. Do not expect to come down quickly.
